```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

**Status.** Carries question R3 ("Is it just plant size?"). The inferential results quoted in the
caption come from the size-adjusted model in `02_Allometry_Gate.Rmd`. Its size-adjusted
`Poly:Inoc:Water` test is **CONFIRMATORY #1**. The size-adjusted cell contrasts and the slope
checks below are **EXPLORATORY** descriptions (n = 5 per cell).

**What the lines are.** The lines are **not** separate regressions per group. They are the fitted
values of the one model the gate uses, `log(grain) ~ log(size) + Stand * Inoculation * Water`:
a single common slope, shifted up or down by group. The vertical gap between a filled and an open
line in a panel is the size-adjusted inoculation effect. Each line is drawn only across its own
group's observed size range, so nothing implies extrapolation, and there are no ribbons (the
elevation contrasts and their CIs are in the caption). An earlier version of this figure fit a
free line to each group's five points; that contradicted the model and is explained in the
section on slopes below.

**Encoding (same in every figure).** Color = stand type (orange = monoculture, blue = intercrop);
filled symbol and solid line = inoculated, open symbol and dashed line = sterile.

```{r libs}
library(tidyverse)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
source("../fig_style.R")

wheat <- readRDS("../wheat_audited.rds") %>%
  mutate(Poly = factor(Poly, c("Mono", "Inter")))
stopifnot(nrow(wheat) == 60, all(wheat$berry > 0), all(wheat$veg > 0))
```

# Numbers for the caption

The same models as `02_Allometry_Gate.Rmd` (and `08.6`): unadjusted `berry_alloc` vs. the
common-slope size-adjusted model on log grain mass.

```{r numbers}
wc <- wheat %>% mutate(log_berry = log(berry), log_veg = log(veg))
m_base <- lm(berry_alloc ~ Poly * Inoc * Water, data = wc)
m_adj  <- lm(log_berry ~ log_veg + Poly * Inoc * Water, data = wc)
p3_unadj <- car::Anova(m_base, type = 2)["Poly:Inoc:Water", "Pr(>F)"]
p3_adj   <- car::Anova(m_adj,  type = 2)["Poly:Inoc:Water", "Pr(>F)"]
slope    <- unname(coef(m_adj)["log_veg"])

# size-adjusted Inoc - Strl contrast in each cell, as % change in grain mass at equal size
adj <- emmeans(m_adj, ~ Inoc | Poly * Water) %>%
  contrast("pairwise", by = c("Poly", "Water"), adjust = "none") %>%
  summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>% as.data.frame()
stopifnot(all(adj$contrast == "Inoc - Strl"))
adj <- adj %>% transmute(Poly, Water, pct = (exp(estimate) - 1) * 100,
                         lo = (exp(lower.CL) - 1) * 100, hi = (exp(upper.CL) - 1) * 100, p = p.value)
knitr::kable(adj %>% mutate(across(c(pct, lo, hi), ~ round(.x, 1)), p = signif(p, 3)),
             caption = "EXPLORATORY - size-adjusted (common-slope) Inoc - Strl effect on grain mass, % change at equal vegetative mass")

# common slope with its CI, and the joint test of slope heterogeneity
slope_ci <- confint(m_adj)["log_veg", ]
m_het    <- lm(log_berry ~ log_veg * Poly * Inoc * Water, data = wc)
het      <- anova(m_adj, m_het)
p_het    <- het$`Pr(>F)`[2]; F_het <- het$F[2]; df_het <- c(het$Df[2], het$Res.Df[2])
A_het    <- car::Anova(m_het, type = 2)
p_veg_inoc  <- A_het["log_veg:Inoc", "Pr(>F)"]
p_veg_water <- car::Anova(lm(log_berry ~ log_veg * Water, data = wc), type = 2)["log_veg:Water", "Pr(>F)"]

# size overlap in the headline panel
ms <- wheat %>% filter(Poly == "Mono", Water == "Severe")
rng <- ms %>% group_by(Inoc) %>% summarise(lo = min(veg), hi = max(veg), .groups = "drop")
r_i <- rng[rng$Inoc == "Inoc", ]; r_s <- rng[rng$Inoc == "Strl", ]
n_strl_in_inoc <- sum(ms$Inoc == "Strl" & ms$veg >= r_i$lo & ms$veg <= r_i$hi)
n_inoc_in_strl <- sum(ms$Inoc == "Inoc" & ms$veg >= r_s$lo & ms$veg <= r_s$hi)
strl_in_range <- ms$veg[ms$Inoc == "Strl" & ms$veg >= r_i$lo & ms$veg <= r_i$hi]
stopifnot(length(strl_in_range) == 1)
sev <- adj %>% filter(Poly == "Mono", Water == "Severe")

# sensitivity: how much of the grain deficit could size alone explain, for any slope in the CI?
gm <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x)))
size_ratio <- gm(ms$veg[ms$Inoc == "Inoc"])   / gm(ms$veg[ms$Inoc == "Strl"])     # inoculated / sterile size
obs_ratio  <- gm(ms$berry[ms$Inoc == "Inoc"]) / gm(ms$berry[ms$Inoc == "Strl"])   # inoculated / sterile grain
sens <- tibble(which = c("lower 95% limit", "point estimate", "upper 95% limit"),
               slope = c(slope_ci[[1]], unname(coef(m_adj)["log_veg"]), slope_ci[[2]])) %>%
  mutate(size_alone = (size_ratio^slope - 1) * 100)
cat(sprintf("Mono x Severe: inoculated plants %.0f%% larger (geometric mean); observed grain %.0f%% (raw geometric means).\n",
            (size_ratio - 1) * 100, (obs_ratio - 1) * 100))
knitr::kable(sens %>% transmute(`slope in the 95% CI` = which, slope = round(slope, 2),
                                `grain change expected from size alone (%)` = round(size_alone, 1)),
             caption = "EXPLORATORY - grain change the size difference alone would produce in Mono x Severe, across the slope's 95% CI")

# how much horizontal spread does each group have? (why per-group slopes are not estimable)
spread <- wheat %>% group_by(Poly, Water, Inoc) %>%
  summarise(`min (g)` = min(veg), `max (g)` = max(veg), `fold-span (max/min)` = max(veg) / min(veg), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(Poly, Water, Inoc)
knitr::kable(spread %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))),
             caption = "Vegetative-mass range in each group of five pots")
cat(sprintf("Slope heterogeneity: joint F(%d, %d) = %.2f, p = %.2f; log_veg:Inoc alone p = %.3f; pooled log_veg x Water p = %.3f.\n",
            df_het[1], df_het[2], F_het, p_het, p_veg_inoc, p_veg_water))
cat(sprintf("Common slope = %.2f (95%% CI %.2f to %.2f).\n", slope, slope_ci[[1]], slope_ci[[2]]))
```

# Figure 2

```{r figure, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6, dpi=150}
poly_strip <- c(Mono = "Monoculture", Inter = "Wheat/ fava intercrop")
strip_lab <- labeller(Poly = poly_strip, Water = water_lab)

# Fitted values of the ONE common-slope model, each group's line drawn only over its own observed
# size range (no extrapolation). Back-transformed to grams so the axes read in grams.
fit_lines <- wc %>%
  group_by(Poly, Inoc, Water) %>%
  summarise(lo = min(log_veg), hi = max(log_veg), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rowwise() %>% mutate(log_veg = list(seq(lo, hi, length.out = 25))) %>% ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::unnest(log_veg) %>%
  mutate(fit = predict(m_adj, newdata = pick(everything())),
         veg = exp(log_veg), berry = exp(fit))

# tint the one panel that carries the finding (Monoculture x Severe)
hl <- tibble(Poly = factor("Mono", levels(wheat$Poly)), Water = factor("Severe", levels(wheat$Water)))
note <- hl %>% mutate(x = 1.0, y = 3.0, label = "")

fig2 <- ggplot(wheat, aes(x = veg, y = berry, color = Poly, shape = Inoc, linetype = Inoc)) +
  geom_rect(data = hl, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = pal_poly[["Mono"]], alpha = 0.07) +
  geom_line(data = fit_lines, aes(group = interaction(Poly, Inoc, Water)), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, stroke = 0.9, fill = NA) +
  geom_text(data = note, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.3, color = "grey20", lineheight = 0.95) +
  facet_grid(Poly ~ Water, labeller = strip_lab) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 4, 6)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2), labels = c("0.05", "0.1", "0.25", "0.5", "1", "2")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_poly, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shp_inoc, labels = inoc_lab) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = lty_inoc, labels = inoc_lab) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.035, 3.2), xlim = c(0.95, 7)) +
  guides(shape    = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = "grey25")),
         linetype = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = "grey25"))) +
  labs(x = "Vegetative mass per plant (g, log scale)",
       y = "Grain mass per plant (g, log scale)") +
  theme_ms() +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey93", linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.spacing = unit(0.9, "lines"))
print(fig2)

dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("figures/Fig2_Allometry.pdf", fig2, width = 9.5, height = 6)
ggsave("figures/Fig2_Allometry.png", fig2, width = 9.5, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## Presentation version: monoculture x severe drought only

The panel that carries the claim, blown up, with larger points and type for a slide. It uses the
**same model and the same fitted lines** as the full figure (one common slope, each line drawn over
its own group's observed size range). The vertical gap between the two lines is the size-adjusted
inoculation effect (EXPLORATORY); it is quoted in the footnote below, not drawn on the plot.

```{r figure-presentation, fig.width=10, fig.height=6.5, dpi=120}
col_mono <- pal_poly[["Mono"]]

# the one panel
pts_ms   <- wheat %>% filter(Poly == "Mono", Water == "Severe")
lines_ms <- fit_lines %>% filter(Poly == "Mono", Water == "Severe")

fig2_pres <- ggplot(pts_ms, aes(x = veg, y = berry, shape = Inoc, linetype = Inoc)) +
  geom_line(data = lines_ms, aes(group = Inoc), color = col_mono, linewidth = 1.8) +
  geom_point(color = col_mono, size = 6, stroke = 1.8, fill = NA) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shp_inoc, labels = inoc_lab) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = lty_inoc, labels = inoc_lab) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 1.5, 2, 3)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4), labels = c("0.05", "0.1", "0.2", "0.4")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.95, 3.1), ylim = c(0.035, 0.6)) +
  guides(shape    = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = col_mono, size = 5), keywidth = unit(2.4, "lines")),
         linetype = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = col_mono), keywidth = unit(2.4, "lines"))) +
  labs(title = "Monoculture, severe drought (40% FC)",
       x = "Vegetative mass per plant (g, log scale)",
       y = "Grain mass per plant (g, log scale)") +
  theme_ms(base_size = 20) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 23, hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 10)),
        plot.title.position = "plot",
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey93", linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 21), axis.text = element_text(size = 18),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 19), plot.margin = margin(10, 14, 6, 6))
print(fig2_pres)

ggsave("figures/Fig2b_MonoSevere_Presentation.pdf", fig2_pres, width = 10, height = 6.5)
ggsave("figures/Fig2b_MonoSevere_Presentation.png", fig2_pres, width = 10, height = 6.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

**Suggested slide text.** *Inoculated wheat under severe drought: larger plants, much less grain.* Footnote:
*Monoculture, severe drought, n = 5 per group. Lines are one common-slope model fitted to all 60 pots;
size-adjusted effect `r sprintf("%.0f%% (95%% CI %.0f to %.0f%%)", sev$pct, sev$lo, sev$hi)`, exploratory.*

**Notes** The two groups overlap in size only partly (one sterile pot falls inside the
inoculated range), so the vertical gap leans on the common slope; the slope is small, so the size
difference alone could shift grain by only about -13% to +36%, against the observed -69%.

## Why common-slope lines, and what the slopes can and cannot say



**What can be said about slopes.**

* **Heterogeneity.** The joint test of every `log(size)` interaction is
  F(`r df_het[1]`, `r df_het[2]`) = `r round(F_het, 2)`, p = `r round(p_het, 2)`: no evidence that slopes differ. State
  plainly that with n = 5 per cell the design **cannot resolve** slope differences, so a common slope is an
  assumption the data do not contradict, not a demonstrated fact. One term, size x inoculation, is
  nominally significant on its own (p = `r round(p_veg_inoc, 3)`); it is reported in
  `02_Allometry_Gate.Rmd` and not dropped, but one nominal hit among seven terms is weak evidence.
* **The common slope is small and imprecise:** `r round(slope, 2)` (95% CI `r round(slope_ci[[1]], 2)` to
  `r round(slope_ci[[2]], 2)`). This changes what Figure 2 may claim. It does **not** show that grain
  rises with size, and it does not show that severe drought breaks that scaling (pooled size x water
  test p = `r round(p_veg_water, 3)`). Do not read the lines as demonstrating either.
* **Size still cannot explain the result.** In Mono x Severe the inoculated plants are
  `r round((size_ratio - 1) * 100)`% larger. Across the whole 95% CI of the slope, size alone would move grain by only
  `r round(min(sens$size_alone), 0)`% to `r round(max(sens$size_alone), 0)`%, against an observed
  `r round((obs_ratio - 1) * 100)`%. That is the real content of the gate: the grain deficit is far larger than any
  slope compatible with the data could produce from the size difference.

## Draft caption

> **Figure 2. The inoculation effect on grain is not a plant-size effect.** Grain mass against
> vegetative mass per plant (both log scale) for each of the 60 pots, by stand type (rows) and water
> level (columns; FC = field capacity). Filled symbols and solid lines are inoculated pots; open
> symbols and dashed lines are sterile pots. Lines are fitted values from the single size-adjusted
> model (one common slope, `r round(slope, 2)`, 95% CI `r round(slope_ci[[1]], 2)` to `r round(slope_ci[[2]], 2)`, shifted by group), each drawn over its
> own group's observed size range; the vertical gap between lines within a panel is the size-adjusted
> inoculation effect. In monoculture under severe drought (shaded) inoculated plants are larger
> (further right) yet make less grain (lower). At equal size they produced
> `r sprintf("%.0f%% less grain (95%% CI %.0f%% to %.0f%% less)", -sev$pct, -sev$hi, -sev$lo)` than sterile
> plants (exploratory). Adjusting for size does not weaken the result: the three-way interaction
> (Stand x Inoculation x Water) on grain is p = `r signif(p3_unadj, 2)` unadjusted and p = `r signif(p3_adj, 2)` size-adjusted.
> The allometric slope is small and imprecise, so the size difference alone cannot account for the
> grain deficit (see text). **Caveat:** with five pots per group the design cannot resolve differences
> in slope between groups (joint test p = `r round(p_het, 2)`); the common slope is an assumption that the data do
> not contradict. In the shaded panel the two groups overlap in size only
> partly: one sterile pot (`r sprintf("%.2f", strl_in_range)` g) lies within the inoculated pots' size range of
> `r sprintf("%.2f to %.2f g", r_i$lo, r_i$hi)`, so the size-adjusted contrast there leans on the common slope.

## Notes for the Results text

* **Overlap wording.** `08.6` and earlier notes said the two groups occupy non-overlapping size
  ranges in this panel. They overlap partly: in Mono x Severe the inoculated pots span
  `r sprintf("%.2f to %.2f g", r_i$lo, r_i$hi)` and the sterile pots `r sprintf("%.2f to %.2f g", r_s$lo, r_s$hi)`;
  `r n_strl_in_inoc` sterile pot falls inside the inoculated range and `r n_inoc_in_strl` inoculated pots inside the sterile range. The
  extrapolation caveat is real but milder than "no overlap" implied.
* **Do not claim from this figure** that grain scales with size or that drought alters that scaling.
  The slope is imprecise and the size x water test is not significant.
* **Fallback if a reviewer objects to any line.** Plot points with a per-group centroid (mean size,
  mean grain) and error bars in both directions. The message, inoculated plants up and to the right of
  sterile in the shaded panel, is visible from the points alone.
